segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And its darkness lasted for eighteen months,
while every day at noon a little shadowy light would shine.
And everyone decided
that it would never again return to normal.
And the fruits did not ripen in that year,
and the wine tasted like unripe grapes.
On the pestilence that occurred throughout the whole earth at this time.
John of Asia wrote extensively about this pestilence, which occurred in the year 855
of the Greeks (544 of our Lord?).
Zacharias also wrote:
that it began first among the interior peoples of the southeast,
namely India, Kush, the Himyarites, and the rest;
and it reached the upper countries in the west:
the peoples of the Romans, the Italians, the Gauls, and the Spaniards.
And it was heard that people were going mad, losing their senses, and biting one another,
and going out into the mountains,
and destroying themselves.
Then the plague came to the regions of Kush that are on the border of Egypt;
and from there it began in Egypt,
and reached Alexandria.
And it spread over Libya, Palestine, Phoenicia, Arabia, and Africa;
and it reached Galatia, Cappadocia, Armenia, and Antioch;
and later on, to the land of the Persians,
and to the peoples in the northeast.
Livestock were seen abandoned, scattered, and wandering about,
with no one to gather them;
fields full of grain,
and no one to harvest;
vineyards whose vintage season had passed,
and no one to pick them.
For human beings had perished,
and scarcely one in a thousand was left.
After three years were completed,
the wrath subsided.
It is said
that when the plague reached the royal city,
it began first among the poor.
And up to sixteen thousand dead were carried out in a single day.
And after the destitute had died,
the destroyer stretched out his hand against the rulers of the world and the prominent.
And those who escaped from sudden death
fell into that affliction of groin tumors, which is boubonos {OCR?},
that is to say, buboes,
and pustules.
And there were also seen in the palms of the hands what looked like three deep drops of blood,
and they would die immediately.
And when people were no longer able to bury the dead,
they would cast the corpses into the sea in heaps upon heaps.
And in the eighteenth year of Justinian, the barbarians conquered Rome, the great city of Italy.
